headline: Perturbation response models are tested for transfer and calibrated reliability
label: Perturbation Response Model Validation
summary: Recent preprints extend perturbation response prediction to new cell lines, combinatorial effects and calibrated evaluation metrics.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how predictive models of perturbation response are validated and how far their outputs carry beyond the fitting setting. The Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 metrics are calibrated on experimental repeats for zero-shot CRISPRi transcriptional response prediction, tying evaluation to measured reproducibility. The CASTER study reports that transferring CRISPRi Perturb-seq knockdown responses across four human cell lines requires screening part of each new line, making transfer conditional rather than automatic. Architectural work includes OCCAM, which combines denoised single-cell representations with gene interaction, text and protein features, and GAIN, which models combinatorial responses as an additive baseline plus a learned interaction term. CIRCE applies Boltzmann distributions over Hamming distance to infer graded signaling activity, and a graph neural network on LINCS L1000 CRISPR profiles nominates perturbation targets with integrated gradients attribution. The shared element across these items is an explicit reliability question, with calibrated metrics and transfer conditions reported alongside predictive performance.
